raw_response:
**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I have been working this land for over forty years. My father farmed it before me. Here in Quzhou, everyone grows winter wheat and summer maize — this rotation is what our land is suited for, what the local grain buyers want, and what I know how to do without hiring outside help. I am 65 now, my back is not what it was, so I am not going to experiment with vegetables or cotton that need constant attention.

I have about 8 mu of flat, irrigated field. I will plant all of it to wheat in autumn, then corn on the same ground after wheat harvest. This is one cycle, one piece of land doing two crops a year — the way it has always been done here.

For wheat, I will buy the improved variety I used last year from the township seed station — it handled the dry spring well. For corn, I will buy a hybrid bag from the cooperative store in the village — everyone buys hybrid corn now, you cannot get the old open-pollinated seeds anymore and the hybrid yields are better anyway.

Fertilizer: I apply base fertilizer before planting and top-dress at tillering for wheat, and sidedress corn at jointing. I follow roughly what the village extension poster says — I cannot read it perfectly but my neighbor explained it to me years ago and I remember. I use urea and a bag of compound fertilizer.

Irrigation: I draw from the village groundwater well. Wheat needs water at sowing, at winter freeze, at jointing, and at heading — that is four times. Corn usually gets one watering at silking if summer rain is short.

Pesticides: I spray herbicide once on wheat in spring and once for leaf disease before heading. On corn I spray herbicide after emergence. I do not spray much more — if it looks bad I might add one more round but I try to keep costs down.

Tillage: After corn harvest I do rotary tillage before seeding wheat — this chops up the corn stalks. After wheat harvest I plant corn directly into the stubble with a seeder, no-till, to save time and moisture.

Expected yield: In a normal year wheat gives me around 450 kg per mu and corn around 550 kg per mu. Last few years have been decent.
